chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who gave the zakat of his wealth, one thousand dirhams, but could not find a place to give that to. So he looked at a slave being sold, whoever wanted him, and bought him with those one thousand dirhams which he had given from his zakat, and freed him. Is that permissible for him? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, there is no problem with that.' I said: 'Suppose when he is freed and becomes free, he trades and becomes a craftsman, and acquires wealth, then he dies and has no heir. So who will inherit him if he has no heir?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The poor believers will inherit him, those who are entitled to the zakat, because he was bought with their money.'
ai.seo_question: Who inherits a freed slave if they die without heirs, when they were purchased using zakat funds?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the use of zakat for 'fi riqab' (freeing slaves) by purchasing and manumitting a slave, establishing a precedent for converting zakat into social capital. The ruling that the freed slave’s estate reverts to the entitled poor believers highlights the concept of collective ownership in zakat distribution, ensuring that the wealth remains within the specific beneficiary class from which it originated.
